conflicts: Brief Alignment proposes: Preserve the complete board, player, two crates, two goals, controls, HUD, and objectives, but make the mechanic relationships explicit. Additional literal detail can increase one-off components and rough exceptions unless each addition is expressed through the established construction system. Clarity proposes: Enlarge the board substantially and pull the controls and objectives closer to its left and right edges, creating one compact gameplay group rather than three distant islands. Changing scale and contrast for hierarchy is useful, but ad hoc emphasis must not introduce unrelated borders, shadows, typography, or spacing. Expressiveness proposes: Give player, crates, lever, door, and targets distinct foundry-specific silhouettes and state changes, introduce purposeful floor wear and heat markings along likely routes, and create one expressive lever-to-door visual linkage while preserving board readability. Extra shapes, textures, glows, and differentiated treatments can fragment palette, geometry, and material logic if each becomes a bespoke exception.
accept: Accept every fidelity restoration, hierarchy correction, and thematic differentiation that can be built from shared grid, type, palette, stroke, radius, elevation, and illustration tokens. Accept stronger focal contrast and a distinctive hero treatment, but keep their construction precise and reuse their rules in related states.
compromise: Implement the craft foundation first: Trim the board container precisely to the 10-column grid and establish one tile-gap, border, and inset-shadow token. Map every required or expressive addition onto a small documented token set, while allowing deliberate scale and color-role differences for hierarchy. Use one exceptional hero treatment at most; all supporting components must share alignment, typography, outline, lighting, and spacing rules, with clipping and viewport-edge defects resolved.
audit_note: Independent persona-preserving MAD cross-critique using the brief, shared r0 screenshot, own critique, and the other three axis suggestions; no moderator output, revised HTML, FUSED/CEN_MAD material, or scores were inspected.
